method: Independent visual inspection with view_image of all eight marked screenshots, all three unmarked original JPEGs, and both supplied exact unenhanced crops; annotations read after image inspection. No inference, enhancement, reconstruction, or public-repository write.

region_recognition.reason: The combination of a pale curved region above a black side wall, the descending pale cord, a gray roughly rectangular patch to its right, and green material at the lower left is recognizably consistent across the views. This is stronger than matching a generic black bag. It supports the same local assembly; it does not establish an exact material point or rigidity.

candidates.reason: Before marker is on the gray/green transition region, toward the left of the gray patch lower portion. The after markers sit at or just below the bottom-left vicinity of the gray patch, near its contact with the dark lower edge. The before view has an irregular, poorly separated gray/green boundary; the marker does not unambiguously select the same bottom-left material corner. Same-region recognition is supported, but calling these centers the same corner is not.
candidates.replacement_reason: Cannot confidently localize the same lower-left material corner from these pixels. A precise replacement would overstate the visible boundary.

candidates.reason: The shifted before center is in the green area below the visible gray patch, with no distinctive corner at its center. The after centers remain at the gray patch lower-left/bottom-edge vicinity. Moving right is superficially plausible, but the added downward displacement is not supported as a corner correction. This rejects the proposed coordinate correction, not identification of the local assembly.
candidates.replacement_reason: Do not publish this shift as a corrected match; the intended lower-left material corner remains unresolved.

candidates.reason: Before and after centers are at the lower-right termination of the gray patch, where its right edge meets its lower edge against black material. The surrounding shape provides a plausible same-feature correspondence in both after images. Blur and the marker width prevent exact edge localization; this is not a certified point match.
candidates.replacement_reason: No visible evidence justifies changing the existing approximate coordinates. Retain the stated uncertainty as an annotation estimate, not a calibrated confidence interval.

candidates.reason: The markers fall near the upper-left start of the gray patch at the sloping upper boundary of the black side wall. The patch extends rightward and downward from this area in both views. This supports a coarse upper-left-feature hypothesis. The bright folded/reflected top boundary and blur leave the exact material junction ambiguous; the highlights themselves should not be treated as a material landmark.
candidates.replacement_reason: No independently better coordinate is apparent. Existing coordinates can remain tentative; no subpixel or uniquely resolved corner is claimed.

limitations: A01 original unresolved and adjusted rejected concern point localization, not a demonstrated wrong-object match.
A02 and A03 supported means worth retaining as approximate visual hypotheses only.
Gray patch is visually recognizable; its exact material, including whether it is reflective tape, is not established by this review.
The adjacent after frames repeat nearly the same view and do not provide an independent before-to-after baseline.
No claim of stationarity, rigid support, alignment, pose, or accepted reconstruction bridge.
No facial identity, biometric correspondence, or bodily landmark used.
recommendation: Preserve original annotations as historical proposals; mark A01 unresolved and do not promote the 15/15 adjustment. Retain A02 and A03 as tentative approximate visual hypotheses. No alignment accepted.
